title: Steering Detection Evasion x Stealthy Misuse: Can a Steered Model Hide That It's Being Steered?

original_idea.body: Build a steering-detector, then find a stealth zone where low-strength harmful steering both works and evades detection, defeating detect-the-steering defenses.

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Concrete covert-misuse threat: defeats detect-the-steering defenses; explicit chain from stealth zone to defense failure.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Build a probe-based detector + sweep harmful steering + measure evasion; guided, novice + mentor feasible.

narrow_scope.reasoning: Focused deliverable but requires building a detector and characterizing a 2D stealth frontier.

counterfactual_value.reasoning: Red-teaming a steering-detection defense is exactly external scrutiny labs deprioritize; no internal access.

low_compute.reasoning: Inference + probe on one small model; single GPU.

novelty.reasoning: Characterizing a harmful-steering stealth-vs-detectability zone appears largely novel.

novelty_assessment.reasoning: The stealth-zone characterization of harmful steering that evades activation detectors is an underexplored angle.
